questions.q_en:
Directions :Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

We sit in the last row, bumped about but free of stares. The bus rolls out of the dull cross roads of the city, and we are soon in the open country side, with fields of sunflowers as far as the eye can see, their heads all facing us. Where there is no water, the land reverts to the desert. While still on level ground, we see in the distance the tall range of the Mount Bogda, abrupt like a shining prism laid horizontally on the desert surface. It is over 5,000 metres high, and the peaks are under permanent snow, in powerful contrast to the flat desert all around. Heaven lake lies part of the way up this range, about 2,000 metres above sea level, at the foot of one of the highest snow-peaks.

As the bus climbs, the sky, brilliant before, grows overcast. I have brought nothing warm to wear. It is all down at the hotel in Urumqi. Rain begins to fall. The man behind me is eating over poweringly smelly goat's cheese. The bus window leaks inhospitably but reveals a beautiful view. We have passed quickly from the desert through arable land to pasture and the ground is now green with grass, the slopes dark with pine. A few cattle drink at a clear stream flowing past moss-covered stones; it is a Constable landscape. The stream changes into a white torrent, and as we climb higher. I wish more and more that I had brought with me something warmer than the pair of shorts that have served me so well in the desert. The stream (which, we are told, rises in Heaven Lake) disappears, and we continue our slow ascent. About noon, we arrive at Heaven Lake, and look for a place to stay at the foot, which is the resort area. We get a room in a small cottage, and I am happy to note that there are thick quilts on the bed.

Standing outside the cottage, we survey our surroundings. Heaven Lake is long, sardine-shaped and fed by snowmelt from a stream at its head. The lake is an intense blue, surrounded on all sides by green mountain walls, dotted with distant sheep. At the head of the lake, beyond the delta of the inflowing stream, is a massive snow-capped peak which dominates the vista; it is part of a series of peaks that culminate, a little out of view, in Mount Bogda itself.

For those who live in the resort, there is a small mess-hall by the shore. We eat here sometimes, and sometimes buy food from the vendors outside, who sell kabab and naan until the last buses leave. The kababs, cooked on skewers over charcoal braziers, are particularly good; highly spiced and well-done. Horse's milk is available too from the local Kazakh herdsmen, but I decline this. I am so affected by the cold that Mr.Cao, the relaxed young man who runs the mess, lends me a spare pair of trousers, several sizes too large but more than comfortable. Once I am warm again, I feel a pre-dinner spurt of energy - dinner will belong incoming - and I ask him whether the lake is good for swimming in.

Select an appropriate title for the passage.
questions.solution_en:
The author sees Mount Bogda while on the journey to Lake Heaven. So, 'Journey to Mount Bogda' cannot be an appropriate title.

'Shorts to trousers' is the sub-plot of the story where the author mentions that he only has the pair of shorts and how after reaching the Lake Heaven, Mr. Cao, one who runs the mess, offered him the trousers. So, from options (a) and (b), option (b) is the more appropriate title, as the story is about the author's account of the visit to Lake Heaven.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

'Peasant Life' is completely out of context to be the title of the given passage.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The new software ______ extensively to ensure its compatibility with various devices.
questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is 'is being tested'. "Is being tested" is the present progressive tense, which indicates that the action of testing the new software is currently ongoing. This choice effectively communicates that the testing process is happening at the present moment.

Option (b) is grammatically incorrect because it combines the present tense "is" with "been testing." In English, the present progressive tense is formed using "is being" followed by the present participle (-ing form) of the verb, as in "is being tested." "Is been testing" does not follow this pattern and is not grammatically valid.

Option (c) is incorrect because it uses the present participle "being" with the present perfect auxiliary verb "has." The present perfect tense is formed with "has been" followed by the past participle of the verb. The correct form for the present perfect tense in this context would be "has been tested."

Option (d) is incorrect. The verb "was" is in the past tense, indicating that the action occurred in the past. However, the phrase "being testing" is a present progressive form, indicating ongoing action in the present. Combining a past tense verb with a present progressive form creates tense inconsistency. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Note:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.q_en:
Directions: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Professionalism is probably the _____ (A) theoretical of the types of soft skills, and certainly the most dependent on context. What professionalism ______ (B) in one organization can be very different from what it means in another. In general, what most employers mean when they say they are _______ (C) for professionalism is someone who understands how they as an individual affect the ______ (D) as a whole. That can mean anything from personal performance related to broad standards, or how one's ______ (E) impacts the health of the team.

Select the appropriate word to fill blank C.
questions.solution_en:
The blank requires a verb that denotes the action done by employers with respect to professionalism. The verb has to be either in Past participle form (V3) or continuous/present participle form (V4) to be used along with the auxiliary verb 'are'. 'Reward' and 'expect' are in base forms of the verbs (V1), so they are negated. 'Awarding' (give or order the giving of (something) as an official payment, compensation, or prize to (someone)) is a contextually irrelevant option as it makes the sentence meaningless if used, so it is negated. 'Looking' when used along with the preposition 'for' means 'hope or expect to find or obtain a particular type of person or thing' and indicates the thing that employers do with respect to professionalism in a person.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take a position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Although the mountaineer was very weak, / he was determined to reach the summit / without nobody's assistance.
options_en: he was determined to reach the summit
Although the mountaineer was very weak
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the part "without nobody's assistance". This creates a double negative, which is grammatically incorrect in standard English. 'Without' is a negative preposition, and 'nobody's' is a negative pronoun. Using two negatives in the same clause makes the meaning positive (e.g., 'not having no help' would logically mean 'having some help'), which contradicts the intended meaning.

To correct this, one of the negatives should be replaced with a positive equivalent. We can either say 'with nobody's assistance' or 'without anybody's assistance'. The latter is more suitable here.

Correct Sentence: Although the mountaineer was very weak, he was determined to reach the summit without anybody's assistance.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. In this model, resources are kept in use for as long as possible, extracting the maximum value from them while in use, then recovering and regenerating products at the end of each service life.

B. The circular economy is a systemic approach to economic development designed to benefit businesses, society, and the environment by moving away from a linear 'take-make-dispose' model.

C. It is based on three core principles: designing out waste and pollution, keeping products and materials in use, and regenerating natural systems for long-term sustainability.

D. Such a transition represents a fundamental shift that requires redesigning products, business models, and supply chains to create a closed-loop system of production and consumption.
questions.solution_en:
The correct sequence is BCAD. Sentence B is the ideal opening as it defines the central concept, "The circular economy," and contrasts it with the traditional linear model. Sentence C logically follows by elaborating on the "three core principles" upon which this economic system is based. Sentence A then explains the practical application of these principles, describing how, "in this model", resources are managed to maximize their value and lifespan. Finally, sentence D provides a concluding statement on the scale of the change, explaining that "Such a transition" requires a fundamental redesign of our entire production and consumption system.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 5 Questions]: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Biogas is a type of gas that can be (1)_____ to produce energy. It causes less harm to the environment than burning coal or oil. Biogas is produced by breaking (2)_____ a plant or animal resource such as cow dung in an oxygen-free environment. Biogas is produced by special microorganisms that can survive and (3)_____ without oxygen. Recently, nanoparticles have been used to make more biogas. Nanoparticles have unique (4)_____ such as their extremely small size and their ability to (5)_____ react with substances.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.solution_en:

questions.q_en: Describe how you will say to a stranger You are trespassing on our property in passive voice.
options_en: Our property was being trespassed by you.
Our property will be trespassed by you.
Our property is trespassed by you.
Our property is being trespassed on by you.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb 'being' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Continuous.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

A document is being typed by Arnab. (Passive Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.q_en:
Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

The project has been progressing steadily for last summer, marked by significant milestones achieved by our dedicated team.
questions.solution_en:
The error is in segment (b) "steadily for last summer." The phrase "for last summer" is incorrect because "last summer" refers to a time in the past. The correct expression should use "since" to indicate the starting point of the progress. "For" is rather used to show a period of time, in the past, present or future. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The corrected sentence: The project has been progressing steadily since last summer, marked by significant milestones achieved by our dedicated team.

questions.q_en:
Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. Identify the part that has an error. Select the option that has an error.

The supervisor was not pleased about him arriving late to the mandatory safety briefing for the third time this month.
questions.solution_en:
When a pronoun comes before a gerund (a verb ending in "-ing" that acts as a noun), the pronoun should be in the possessive case. The action the supervisor was not pleased about was the "arriving," so the pronoun should show possession of that action.

So, the phrase "pleased about him arriving late" should be replaced with "pleased about his arriving late".

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options_en: A better work-life balance are being demanding by employees.
A better work-life balance is demanding by employees.
A better work-life balance is being demanded by employees.
A better work-life balance are been demanded by employees.
questions.solution_en:
Options a) and d) are incorrect as they use the plural verb 'are' for the singular subject 'work-life balance'. It is a violation of the subject-verb agreement.

'Is demanding' is the construct for the active voice, but in the given sentence in option b), 'work-life balance' is the receiver of the action, so the passive voice construct should have been used here. So, option b) is incorrect too.

Option (c) is both grammatically and contextually correct.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.

Emotional stimulation provides the necessary __________ for creative imagination. (fecundity)
questions.solution_en:
"Fecundity" means the ability to produce or be fertile, especially in a creative or intellectual sense. "Fertility" is the closest synonym, fitting the context of creative imagination.

Fecundity: Productiveness, especially creatively or intellectually.

Fertility: The quality of being productive or fertile.

Freedom: Liberty, unrelated.

Fulcrum: A pivot point, irrelevant.

Force: Strength or power, not specific to creativity.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).
